title: Harpagide alleviates neuroinflammation and cognitive dysfunction in sepsis-associated encephalopathy: Association with the MMP9/NF-kappaB signaling pathway.
authors: Lou, Fen; Deng, Guochun; Chen, Jiejuan; Jing, Yijiang; Wang, Ao; Zhang, Mazhong; Zhang, Yongping; Wang, Bin
one_liner_zh: 该文研究Harpagide对脓毒症相关脑病的神经保护作用，涉及MMP9/NF-kappaB信号通路，虽含分子对接与MD模拟，但核心是药物-蛋白互作而非蛋白质-DNA互作，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Sepsis-associated encephalopathy (SAE) is a severe neurological complication of sepsis, characterized by uncontrolled neuroinflammation and cognitive decline, yet no specific therapy is currently available. Harpagide, a naturally occurring iridoid glycoside, has been reported to possess anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective activities; however, its therapeutic potential in SAE remains unexplored. This study aimed to investigate whether Harpagide exerts neuroprotective effects in SAE and to elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms. METHODS: A mouse model of SAE was established by intraperitoneal injection of lipopolysaccharide (LPS, 18 mg/kg). Cognitive performance was assessed using behavioral assays. Brain tissue morphology and neuronal survival were evaluated through histopathological examination. Glial cell activation and the production of pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-alpha, IL-1beta, IL-6) were measured. Network pharmacology was employed to predict potential targets, followed by molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations to predict binding interactions with core targets. Western blotting was performed to determine the expression levels of key proteins involved in the MMP9/NF-kappaB signaling pathway. RESULTS: Treatment with Harpagide significantly improved behavioral performance, ameliorated brain pathological changes, preserved hippocampal neurons, suppressed glial activation, and reduced the levels of TNF-alpha, IL-1beta, and IL-6 in SAE mice. Network pharmacology analysis predicted four core targets: GAPDH, CASP3, MMP9, and ICAM1. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations suggested stable binding between Harpagide and MMP9. Western blot analysis further showed that Harpagide treatment was associated with reduced expression of MMP9 and phosphorylated NF-kappaB p65 in both hippocampal and cortical tissues. CONCLUSIONS: The present study demonstrates that Harpagide exerts neuroprotective effects in SAE, which are associated with mitigated neuroinflammation and reduced MMP9/NF-kappaB signaling, supporting its potential as a promising therapeutic candidate for this devastating condition.
abstract_zh: 背景：脓毒症相关性脑病（SAE）是脓毒症的一种严重神经系统并发症，其特征为失控的神经炎症和认知功能下降，但目前尚无特异性治疗方法。哈帕格苷（Harpagide）是一种天然存在的环烯醚萜苷，据报道具有抗炎和神经保护活性；然而，其在SAE中的治疗潜力尚未被探索。本研究旨在探讨哈帕格苷是否在SAE中发挥神经保护作用，并阐明其潜在分子机制。方法：通过腹腔注射脂多糖（LPS，18 mg/kg）建立SAE小鼠模型。使用行为学实验评估认知表现。通过组织病理学检查评估脑组织形态和神经元存活情况。测量胶质细胞活化及促炎细胞因子（TNF-α、IL-1β、IL-6）的产生。采用网络药理学预测潜在靶点，随后进行分子对接和分子动力学模拟以预测与核心靶点的结合相互作用。通过蛋白质印迹法测定MMP9/NF-κB信号通路中关键蛋白的表达水平。结果：哈帕格苷治疗显著改善了SAE小鼠的行为表现，减轻了脑病理变化，保护了海马神经元，抑制了胶质细胞活化，并降低了TNF-α、IL-1β和IL-6的水平。网络药理学分析预测了四个核心靶点：GAPDH、CASP3、MMP9和ICAM1。分子对接和分子动力学模拟提示哈帕格苷与MMP9之间存在稳定结合。蛋白质印迹分析进一步显示，哈帕格苷治疗与海马和皮层组织中MMP9及磷酸化NF-κB p65表达降低相关。结论：本研究证明哈帕格苷在SAE中发挥神经保护作用，这些作用与减轻神经炎症和降低MMP9/NF-κB信号传导相关，支持其作为这种破坏性疾病的有前景治疗候选药物的潜力。
